text_version.title: Dhammapada
text_version.summary: The Dhammapada is a collection of aphorisms in Pali arranged by theme. It is one of the most widely read and best-known works in the Pali canon.

person_roles.note: Aphorisms attributed to the Buddha in the Khuddaka Nikāya.

text_version.title: Mūlapariyāya Sutta (MN 1)
text_version.summary: The Root of All Things, the first sutta of the Majjhima Nikāya. This sutta discusses how different beings approach the root of phenomena.

person_roles.note: Opening sutta of the Majjhima Nikāya.

text_version.title: Sāmaññaphala Sutta (DN 2)
text_version.summary: The Fruits of the Contemplative Life, discusses the benefits of renunciate practice.

person_roles.note: Second sutta of the Dīgha Nikāya.

text_version.title: Anattalakkhaṇa Sutta (SN 22.59)
text_version.summary: The Discourse on the Characteristic of Non-self, one of the most famous sermons where the Buddha teaches the five aggregates are not self.

person_roles.note: Key discourse on non-self to the five bhikkhus.

text_version.title: Ariya Aṭṭhaṅgika Magga (AN 8.2)
text_version.summary: The Noble Eightfold Path described in detail in the Aṅguttara Nikāya.

person_roles.note: Explanation of the eight factors of the path.
